newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran to register presidential election candidates.
newsitem.headline: Iran to register presidential election candidates.

text.p: Iran will start on Thursday registering candidates for its presidential elections next month, Iranian Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati said on Wednesday.

Besharati said the candidates would have until Monday to sign up at the interior ministry for the May 23 polls which will elect a successor to President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, Iranian state television said.

The list of candidates would be handed over on Tuesday to the Guardian Council, an election screening body of lawyers and Shi'ite Moslem clerics, which would announce the approved candidates within 10 days, Besharati added.
About a dozen candidates have said they would register to run in the elections. The Guardian Council has in past polls disqualified all but a handful of those who signed up.

Although Iran's constitution says only prominent political or religious men can become candidates, a female former member of parliament has also announced her intention to join the race. She has said she hoped her candidacy would lead to a legal interpretation by the Guardian Council allowing women to run.
Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, backed by conservatives who hold a majority in the assembly, appears to be the leading candidate.

Mohammad Khatami, a former minister of culture and Islamic guidance, is another strong candidate. He is backed by a pro-Rafsanjani centrist group and radical Islamist intellectuals who have moderated many of their views in the past few years.
Rafsanjani is barred by the constitution from running after two consecutive four-year terms.
